CVE-2026-11940.title:
tarfile.extractall() with the 'data' or 'tar'
 filter could be by ...
CVE-2026-11940.description:
tarfile.extractall() with the 'data' or 'tar'
 filter could be bypassed by a crafted archive where a hardlink 
references a symlink stored at a deeper name than the hardlink itself.  
The extraction fallback validated the symlink at it's archived location 
but recreated it at the hardlink's shallower
path, letting a relative
 target the filter judged contained escape the destination directory.  
This allowed a malicious tar archive to create a symlink pointing 
outside the destination, enabling out-of-destination file reads or 
writes. This was an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-4330.

CVE-2026-15308.title: The incremental HTML parser (html.parser.HTMLParser) allows for C ...
CVE-2026-15308.description:
The incremental HTML parser (html.parser.HTMLParser) allows for CPU
denial-of-service through repeated unterminated markup declarations when
processing uncontrolled data.

CVE-2026-19445.title: A remote, unauthenticated TLS client can make a server crash or c ...
CVE-2026-19445.description:
A remote, unauthenticated TLS client can make a server crash or call
through a freed pointer if its sni_callback assigns a different context to
SSLSocket.context (the documented way to select a certificate per server
name) and nothing else keeps the original ssl.SSLContext alive. Typical
cases are servers that create an SSLContext per connection or replace it
while connections are open; servers that wrap their listening socket with
it are not affected.


Mitigation: keep a reference to every SSLContext that sets sni_callback for
the lifetime of the server. TLS clients are not affected.

CVE-2026-19553.title: ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio() didn't require the server_hostname argu ...
CVE-2026-19553.description:
ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio() didn't require the server_hostname argument
to not be None if ssl.SSLContext.check_hostname was set. Due to a
missing parameter check in SSLObject, if the server_hostname argument
isn't supplied then hostname verification would be silently skipped.


This defect could lead to programs where certificate hostname verification
*appeared* to be succeeding with SSLContext.check_hostname = True and no
ValueError being raised due to misconfiguration.


If the program passes a server_hostname value that isn't an empty string
or None to any of these APIs then certificate hostname verification
proceeds as expected and the program is not affected by this vulnerability.


Mitigating this vulnerability doesn't require updating Python or applying
the patch. To mitigate, pass a valid non-None and non-empty
server_hostname value to SSLContext.wrap_bio(),
asyncio.create_connection(), or asyncio.loop.start_tls() and
certificate hostname verification will proceed as expected. Upgrading to
the latest version of Python or applying the patch only changes the
behavior from silently skipping hostname verification to raising a
ValueError, similar to SSLContext.wrap_socket(), when server_hostname
isn't supplied.

CVE-2026-6019.title: http.cookies.Morsel.js_output() returns an inline <script> snippe ...
CVE-2026-6019.description: http.cookies.Morsel.js_output() returns an inline <script> snippet and only escapes " for JavaScript string context. It does not neutralize the HTML parser-sensitive sequence </script> inside the generated script element. Mitigation base64-encodes the cookie value to disallow escaping using cookie value.

CVE-2026-103995.title: Response body and chunk parsing would handle non-hex or negative  ...
CVE-2026-103995.description: Response body and chunk parsing would handle non-hex or negative integers incorrectly which could result in misinterpreting HTTP response contents.

CVE-2026-115559.title: IMAP4.starttls() wraps the socket in TLS but leaves self._readbuf ...
CVE-2026-115559.description: IMAP4.starttls() wraps the socket in TLS but leaves self._readbuf, imaplib's own read-ahead buffer, untouched. Any plaintext bytes that arrived in the same recv() as the tagged OK to STARTTLS are returned by readline() after the handshake, so the client treats them as the first responses on the protected channel. A network attacker who cannot break TLS can append forged lines after the server's OK, let the handshake complete with the real server and a valid certificate, and have the client accept the forged CAPABILITY and the forged tagged completion of the next command. This is the STARTTLS command/response injection class of CVE-2011-0411.

CVE-2026-115791.title:
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to

 ...
CVE-2026-115791.description:
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to

decompress an archive, a Python script shadowing the stdlib can be

created. Then if an error occurs during decompressing the next file,

the newly created Python script is executed. This is especially true

if the created Python is called traceback.py. The problem is that

Python adds the current directory to sys.path when python -m MODULE is

run, and the archive is also decompressed in the current directory.



The fix removes sys.path[0] in gzip, tarfile and zipfile command line

interface to prevent shadowing standard library modules from extracted

files.

CVE-2026-116566.description: socket.getaddrinfo() previously accepted null bytes within *host* and *port* parameters which can cause the values to be silently truncated.

CVE-2026-119170.title: There was a regression in how FIPS algorithms were enforced for t ...
CVE-2026-119170.description: There was a regression in how FIPS algorithms were enforced for the hashlib module. Only users that are using OpenSSL in FIPS mode are affected. Only Python 3.14.10 is affected, all other Python versions are unaffected.

CVE-2026-124249.title: http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response  ...
CVE-2026-124249.description:
http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response carried an
already expired Set-Cookie header for it, using the Domain and Path
attributes from the header without consulting the cookie policy. A server
could therefore delete cookies belonging to other domains from a shared
cookie jar, such as the one used by urllib's HTTPCookieProcessor. The fix
consults the cookie policy before an expired cookie may delete an existing
one, as required by RFC 6265 section 5.3.
